definition_zh: 肺炎；肺部炎症；急性肺部感染
definition_en: an infection or inflammation of the lungs that fills the air sacs with fluid and makes breathing hard
core_image: 肺泡里积了水，每次呼吸都像隔着湿棉花吹气
scene: 冬夜里，老人咳出一口带血的痰，额头烧得发烫。The doctor heard crackles in his chest and sent him to hospital with pneumonia.
sceneCN: 这里 pneumonia 是「急性肺部感染」（第 2 个义项：发烧、咳嗽、需要就医的那一种肺炎）；句意为医生听出他胸中的湿啰音，以肺炎把他送进了医院。

collocations.zh: 轻型肺炎（仍能下地行走的非典型肺炎）

derivatives.zh: 肺的；肺炎的；由 pneumon（肺）加 -ic 构成
肺组织的炎症；pneumon 加 -itis（炎症），所指比肺炎更窄
支气管肺炎；由 bronch-（气管）与 pneumonia 复合而成

senses.title: Inflammation of the lungs
senses.definition: any inflammation of the lung tissue, whatever germ or irritant has caused it
senses.definitionCN: 不论由何种病菌或刺激物引起，肺组织出现的炎症
senses.example: Pneumonia can follow a viral infection or appear on its own.
senses.exampleCN: 肺炎可能继发于病毒感染，也可能单独出现。
senses.why: Greek pneumon named the lung as the breathing organ, and the ending -ia named a condition of it, so the word first described a diseased lung rather than a germ.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 pneumon 把肺命名为「呼吸的器官」，词尾 -ia 表示某种状态，所以这个词最初描述的是「有病的肺」，而不是某种病菌。

senses.title: The acute infectious illness
senses.definition: a sudden infection of the lungs with fever, cough and chest pain, usually needing medical treatment
senses.definitionCN: 以发热、咳嗽和胸痛为表现的急性肺部感染，通常需要就医治疗
senses.example: He was admitted with pneumonia after two days of high fever.
senses.exampleCN: 高烧两天之后，他因肺炎住进了医院。
senses.why: Once doctors learned that germs cause it, the same word came to name the illness a patient actually feels, with its fever and its cough.
senses.whyCN: 当医生弄清了病菌才是病因，同一个词就开始命名患者真正感受到的那场病，连同它的发热与咳嗽。

senses.title: A single infected lobe
senses.definition: one localized area of infected lung tissue, as seen on a chest image or heard through a stethoscope
senses.definitionCN: 某一肺叶或某一片肺组织上的感染病灶，可在胸片或听诊中定位
senses.example: The scan showed pneumonia in the lower lobe of the right lung.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示右肺下叶有肺炎病灶。
senses.why: Because the infection often settles in one lobe, doctors use the same noun for the patch as for the whole disease.
senses.whyCN: 因为感染常常落在一个肺叶里，医生就用同一个名词既指那片病灶，也指整个疾病。

senses.title: Walking pneumonia
senses.definition: a mild form of pneumonia in which the patient stays active and the symptoms are easily mistaken for a cold
senses.definitionCN: 症状较轻、患者仍能活动、容易被当成感冒的一种肺炎
senses.example: Walking pneumonia rarely puts a healthy adult to bed.
senses.exampleCN: 轻型肺炎很少让健康的成年人卧床。
senses.why: The nickname was coined because these patients could still walk about, so the illness hid behind its mildness.
senses.whyCN: 这个绰号来自患者仍能四处走动，于是疾病就藏在轻微的症状后面。

senses.title: The friend of the aged
senses.titleCN: 终末期肺炎；旧称「老人的朋友」
senses.definition: pneumonia seen as the last illness of a frail elderly person, sometimes described as a short and merciful ending
senses.definitionCN: 体弱老人临终时所患的肺炎，旧时被说成一种短暂而少折磨的结局
senses.example: Old doctors sometimes called pneumonia the friend of the aged.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的医生有时把肺炎称作「老人的朋友」。
senses.why: In an age without antibiotics, pneumonia could close a long illness quickly, so the word carried a strange comfort as well as fear.
senses.whyCN: 在没有抗生素的年代，肺炎能很快结束一场漫长的病，于是这个词既带着恐惧，也带着一点奇怪的安慰。

intro.en: Pneumonia comes from Greek pneumon, the lung, a word itself built on pneuma, breath or air.
intro.cn: pneumonia 来自希腊语 pneumon（肺），而这个词本身又由 pneuma（气息、风）构成。

items.en: A reconstructed root for breathing or blowing is generally thought to lie behind pneuma; the deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为 pneuma 背后有一个表示「呼吸、吹」的原始印欧语重构词根；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Pneuma meant breath, air or wind, and it also named the breath of life.
items.cn: pneuma 指气息、空气或风，也用来指生命的气息。

items.en: Pneumon named the lung, literally the organ of breathing.
items.cn: pneumon 指肺，字面意思就是「用来呼吸的器官」。

items.en: Hippocratic writers used pneumonia for a disease of the lungs, and the -ia ending marked a condition.
items.cn: 希波克拉底学派的作者用 pneumonia 指肺部疾病，-ia 词尾表示某种状态。

items.en: Medical Latin kept the Greek word almost unchanged, including the pn- cluster that English now pronounces without the p.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语几乎原样保留了希腊词，连英语如今不发音的 pn- 也留着。

items.en: English borrowed the Latin term in the seventeenth century, and it has named the disease ever since.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个拉丁词，此后一直用它命名这种病。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the Greek lung root in view, while the near-meaning group sorts pneumonia from the lung diseases it is often confused with.
note.cn: 形近组围绕希腊语「肺」这个词根；近义组则把肺炎与常被混淆的肺部疾病分开。

entries.definition: relating to the lungs or to pneumonia
entries.definitionCN: 与肺或肺炎有关的；由 pneumonia 加 -ic 构成。

entries.definition: inflammation of the lung tissue itself
entries.definitionCN: 肺组织本身的炎症；与 pneumonia 同源，但 -itis 强调炎症而非感染。

entries.definition: worked by air or gas
entries.definitionCN: 靠空气或气体工作的；与肺炎同出 pneuma 一词，词义已转向「气」。

entries.definition: inflammation of the larger airways
entries.definitionCN: 较大气道的炎症，病变在气管分支而不在肺泡。

entries.definition: a bacterial infection that damages the lungs over a long period
entries.definitionCN: 长期损害肺部的细菌感染，病程比肺炎慢得多。

entries.definition: inflammation of the membrane around the lungs
entries.definitionCN: 肺外那层胸膜的炎症，痛在胸侧而不在肺泡里。

normalIntro.en: Pneumonia is a Greek lung word, so its parts point to breath and to the organ that does the breathing.
normalIntro.cn: pneumonia 是希腊语的「肺」词，它的各部分都指向呼吸和负责呼吸的那个器官。

normal.en: The pn- at the start is kept from Greek, so the p is silent and the word begins with a nyu sound.
normal.cn: 开头的 pn- 是从希腊语保留下来的，所以 p 不发音，词从「nyu」这个音开始。

normal.en: Pneumon means lung and -ia means a condition, so pneumonia is a condition of the lung.
normal.cn: pneumon 是肺，-ia 表示某种状态，所以 pneumonia 就是「肺的病态」。

normal.en: Pneumonic is the adjective, and pneumonitis is inflammation of the tissue rather than of the air sacs.
normal.cn: pneumonic 是形容词，pneumonitis 指肺组织的炎症，与肺泡里的肺炎不同。

normal.en: Walking pneumonia is mild enough that the patient keeps walking around.
normal.cn: walking pneumonia 症状轻，患者还能照常走动。

normal.en: Double pneumonia means both lungs are infected, not twice the severity of one lung.
normal.cn: double pneumonia 指两侧肺都受感染，不是单侧病情的两倍。

abstract.en: Picture a sponge soaked with water, and every squeeze makes a wet crackle.
abstract.cn: 想象一块吸满水的海绵，每捏一下都发出湿漉漉的响声。

abstract.en: Imagine a feverish patient propped on pillows, coughing until the chest hurts.
abstract.cn: 想象一位发烧的病人靠着枕头，咳到胸口发痛。

abstract.en: Think of a chest image with one white patch marking the infected lobe.
abstract.cn: 想象一张胸片上有一块白影，标出受感染的那个肺叶。

examples.en: Pneumonia is more dangerous in very young children and in the elderly.
examples.cn: 肺炎在幼儿和老人身上更危险。

examples.en: She recovered from pneumonia after a week of antibiotics.
examples.cn: 用了一周抗生素后，她的肺炎痊愈了。

examples.en: Doctors listen for crackles, one of the signs of pneumonia.
examples.cn: 医生听诊寻找湿啰音，那是肺炎的体征之一。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛摸你呀」——像有人摸一下胸口就让你咳起来，正合肺炎的样子；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 pneuma（气息、风）→ pneumon（肺，即「呼吸的器官」）→ pneumonia（肺病）→ 拉丁语 pneumonia → 英语 pneumonia，核心义「肺里积了水、气换不动」。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a diseased lung, narrows to the acute infection a patient feels, then to the infected patch on an image, to the mild walking form, and finally to the last illness of the very old.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起初指有病的肺，随后收窄为患者能感到的急性感染，再指影像上那片感染灶，又指症状轻微的「可行走」型，最后指高龄者临终时的那场病。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: air sacs filled with fluid, each breath bubbling through wet cotton.
core.cn: 核心意象：肺泡里积满液体，每次呼吸都像隔着湿棉花冒泡。

branches.en: A diseased lung is the oldest medical sense of the word.
branches.cn: 「有病的肺」是这个词最古老的医学义项。

branches.en: The acute infection is what a patient feels as fever and cough.
branches.cn: 急性感染是患者感到的发烧与咳嗽。

branches.en: One infected lobe is the same disease seen on an image.
branches.cn: 单个受感染的肺叶，是同一疾病在影像上的样子。

branches.en: The walking form is the mild end of the same infection.
branches.cn: 「可行走」型是同一感染中较轻的一端。

branches.en: General lung inflammation and the last illness of the aged share one word.
branches.cn: 「肺的炎症」与「老人临终的那场病」共用一个词。

intro.en: Pneumonia joins Greek pneumon, the lung, to the noun ending -ia; English then built pneumonic, pneumonitis and bronchopneumonia on the same stem.
intro.cn: pneumonia 由希腊语 pneumon（肺）加名词词尾 -ia 构成；英语又用同一个词干造出 pneumonic、pneumonitis 与 bronchopneumonia。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer keeps Greek pneumonia and supplies pulmo, the lung, and spirare, to breathe.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层保留了希腊语的 pneumonia，并提供 pulmo（肺）与 spirare（呼吸）。

latinEntries.exampleCN: pulmo 生出 pulmonary 与 pulmonology。
spirare 生出 respire 与 inspiration。

definition_en: a severe headache that often throbs on one side of the head and comes with nausea and a dislike of light
core_image: 一侧太阳穴里藏着一把小锤，光一亮就敲一下
scene: 下午的光线突然变强，她拉上窗帘，抱着头缩进沙发角落。A single bright shaft of light made her migraine worse within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 migraine 是「一次偏头痛发作」（第 2 个义项：正在发生的那一阵头痛）；句意为一道强光在几分钟内就让她的偏头痛加重了。

collocations.zh: 静默型偏头痛（只有先兆、不头痛）

derivatives.zh: 偏头痛的；患偏头痛的；由 migraine 加 -ous 构成
偏头痛患者；借法语 -eur（指人）加在 migraine 之后
抗偏头痛的；anti-（抗）加 migraine，多用于描述药物

senses.title: The recurring headache disorder
senses.titleCN: 偏头痛（反复发作的头痛疾病）
senses.definition: a neurological condition that causes repeated severe headaches, often on one side of the head and often with nausea
senses.definitionCN: 引起反复剧烈头痛的神经系统疾病，痛常在单侧，并常伴恶心
senses.example: Migraine runs in her family, and two of her sisters have it too.
senses.exampleCN: 偏头痛在她家有遗传，她的两个姐妹也有。
senses.why: The Greek name meant half the skull, so the disorder was named for where it hurts rather than for what causes it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原名意为「半边颅骨」，所以这个病是按「痛在哪里」命名的，而不是按病因命名。

senses.title: A single attack
senses.definition: one episode of throbbing pain, usually lasting hours, sometimes with vomiting
senses.definitionCN: 一次搏动性的疼痛发作，通常持续数小时，有时伴呕吐
senses.example: A migraine kept her in a dark room all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 一次偏头痛让她整个下午都待在暗房里。
senses.why: Patients feel the disorder only during an attack, so the same noun names both the illness and the episode.
senses.whyCN: 患者只在发作时才感到这个病，所以同一个词既指疾病，也指那一次发作。

senses.title: Migraine with aura
senses.definition: a migraine preceded by flashing lights, a blind spot or tingling that warns of the coming pain
senses.definitionCN: 在疼痛到来之前出现闪光、视野缺口或刺麻感的偏头痛
senses.example: Her migraine with aura always begins with a zigzag of light.
senses.exampleCN: 她的有先兆偏头痛总是以一道锯齿状的光开始。
senses.why: The warning signals come from the brain itself, so doctors gave the word a subtype that names the visible omen.
senses.whyCN: 这些警告信号来自大脑本身，于是医生给这个词添了一个亚型，专门命名看得见的「前兆」。

senses.title: Silent migraine
senses.definition: an attack with the aura and the nausea but without the headache itself
senses.definitionCN: 有先兆与恶心、却没有头痛本身的一次发作
senses.example: A silent migraine can be mistaken for a stomach upset.
senses.exampleCN: 静默型偏头痛可能被误当成肠胃不适。
senses.why: Because the headache can be absent, the word had to carry a form that describes the attack by its other symptoms.
senses.whyCN: 因为头痛可以缺席，这个词只好多出一个用法，靠其他症状来描述这次发作。

senses.title: The old name for half the head
senses.definition: the older medical name hemicrania, which simply described pain in one half of the head
senses.definitionCN: 较早的医学名称 hemicrania，字面只说「半边头在痛」
senses.example: Old texts called it hemicrania before the French form became migraine.
senses.exampleCN: 在法语形式变成 migraine 之前，旧文献称它为 hemicrania。
senses.why: The modern word is a worn-down French version of the Greek half-head name, so the oldest layer still shows through.
senses.whyCN: 现代这个词是希腊语「半头」之名经法语磨损后的样子，最古老的那一层至今仍透出来。

intro.en: Migraine is the worn-down descendant of Greek hemikrania, a compound of hemi-, half, and kranion, skull.
intro.cn: migraine 是希腊语 hemikrania 磨损后的后代，那个词由 hemi-（一半）与 kranion（颅骨）复合而成。

items.en: Hemi- meant half, and it still halves words such as hemisphere.
items.cn: hemi- 意为「一半」，至今仍把 hemisphere 之类的词一分为二。

items.en: Kranion meant the skull or the head, and it survives in cranium.
items.cn: kranion 指颅骨或头部，至今留在 cranium 一词里。

items.en: Hemikrania named a pain that occupied one half of the head, a term used in Greek medical writing.
items.cn: hemikrania 指占据半边头颅的疼痛，是希腊医学文献里的用语。

items.en: Medical Latin took the Greek term over almost unchanged.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语几乎原样接收了这个希腊词。

items.en: French wore the long word down to migraigne, losing the hemi- that speakers no longer recognised.
items.cn: 法语把这个长词磨成 migraigne，丢掉了听者已不再辨认的 hemi-。

items.en: English borrowed the French form as migrayne, and the modern spelling migraine settled later.
items.cn: 英语借入法语形式 migrayne，现代拼写 migraine 则是后来才固定的。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the half-head root and its modern family, while the near-meaning group places migraine among other headaches.
note.cn: 形近组沿着「半头」这个词根及其现代词族；近义组把偏头痛放进其他头痛之中。

entries.definition: relating to or affected by migraine
entries.definitionCN: 偏头痛的；患偏头痛的；由 migraine 加 -ous 构成。

entries.definition: pain in one half of the head, the old name for migraine
entries.definitionCN: 半边头的疼痛，是偏头痛的旧名；与 migraine 同源。

entries.definition: a person who suffers from migraine
entries.definitionCN: 偏头痛患者；借法语后缀 -eur 指人。

entries.definition: pain in the head from any cause
entries.definitionCN: 任何原因引起的头痛，范围比偏头痛宽得多。

entries.definition: a headache that strikes in short, extremely painful bursts around one eye
entries.definitionCN: 围绕一只眼睛短促爆发的剧痛，属于另一种原发性头痛。

entries.definition: a medical word for headache of any kind
entries.definitionCN: 医学上对任何头痛的称呼，并不专指偏头痛。

normalIntro.en: Migraine is a worn-down Greek phrase for half the skull, so the word itself explains why the pain favours one side.
normalIntro.cn: migraine 是希腊语「半边颅骨」磨损后的样子，词本身就解释了疼痛为何偏爱一侧。

normal.en: Hemi- means half and kranion means skull, so hemicrania is literally half-head pain.
normal.cn: hemi- 是一半，kranion 是颅骨，hemicrania 字面就是「半边头在痛」。

normal.en: French shortened hemicrania to migraigne, and English took that shorter form.
normal.cn: 法语把 hemicrania 缩短成 migraigne，英语取的是这个较短的形式。

normal.en: Migrainous is the adjective, and a migraineur is the person who has the attacks.
normal.cn: migrainous 是形容词，migraineur 指经常发作的那个人。

normal.en: An attack is one episode, while chronic migraine is the pattern of frequent attacks.
normal.cn: an attack 是一次发作，而 chronic migraine 指频繁发作的模式。

normal.en: A silent migraine has the aura without the headache, so the name covers a whole family of attacks.
normal.cn: 静默型偏头痛有先兆而无头痛，可见这个名字覆盖的是一整个发作类型。

abstract.en: Picture a vice closing on one temple while the other side stays free.
abstract.cn: 想象一把虎钳夹住一侧太阳穴，另一侧却毫无感觉。

abstract.en: Imagine a dark room, a cold cloth over the eyes, and a wave of nausea.
abstract.cn: 想象一间暗房、一块敷在眼睛上的冷布，还有一阵恶心。

abstract.en: Think of a zigzag of light crawling across the view before the pain arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象一道锯齿状的光在疼痛到来之前爬过视野。

examples.en: She has had migraines since her teens, usually on the right side.
examples.cn: 她从十几岁起就常犯偏头痛，多发生在右侧。

examples.en: Bright light and skipped meals can trigger a migraine.
examples.cn: 强光和错过吃饭都可能诱发偏头痛。

examples.en: Migraine with aura is often preceded by flashing lights.
examples.cn: 有先兆偏头痛常以闪光作为前奏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「my grain」——像脑袋里有一粒麦子被磨盘来回碾过，碾得半边发痛；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hēmi-（一半）+ kranion（颅骨）→ hēmikrania（半边头之痛）→ 拉丁语 hemicrania → 古法语 migraigne → 英语 migraine，核心义「只痛半边头」。

sensesIntro.en: Migraine names a disorder, then a single attack, then the aura and the headache-free form, and it still carries the Greek half-head description.
sensesIntro.cn: migraine 先指一种疾病，再指一次发作，又指有先兆与无头痛的类型，而它始终带着希腊语「半头」的描述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small hammer behind one temple that strikes whenever light flashes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一侧太阳穴后面藏着一把小锤，光一闪就敲一下。

branches.en: The disorder is the long condition behind every attack.
branches.cn: 疾病是每一次发作背后那个长期存在的状况。

branches.en: One attack is the disorder felt at a single moment.
branches.cn: 一次发作是这种病在某一刻被感受到的样子。

branches.en: The aura is the warning the brain gives before the pain.
branches.cn: 先兆是大脑在疼痛之前给出的警告。

branches.en: Without the headache, the attack shows only its other symptoms.
branches.cn: 头痛缺席时，这次发作只剩下别的症状。

branches.en: The Greek half-head name and the modern disorder describe the same place of pain.
branches.cn: 希腊语的「半头」之名与今天的疾病，说的是同一个疼痛位置。

intro.en: Migraine is the worn-down French descendant of Greek hemikrania, and hemi- still halves many English words.
intro.cn: migraine 是希腊语 hemikrania 经法语磨损后的后代，而 hemi- 至今仍把许多英语词分成两半。

latinIntro.en: Latin kept hemicrania and cranium, and the Latin cranium is the same skull that Greek kranion named.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语保留了 hemicrania 与 cranium，而拉丁语的 cranium 就是希腊语 kranion 所指的那块颅骨。

items.meaningCN: 发作于一侧的反复头痛

items.exampleCN: 偏头痛患者；业余爱好者

latinEntries.example: Hemicrania is the Latin form of the Greek name.
latinEntries.exampleCN: hemicrania 是那个希腊名称的拉丁形式。
cranium 生出 cranial 与 craniology。

definition_en: the state of being unable to sleep, or a lasting difficulty in falling or staying asleep
core_image: 床头的钟走了一整夜，眼睛始终睁着
scene: 连续两周，他每夜只能睡两三个小时，白天靠浓咖啡撑着。By the third week, insomnia had worn him down until he could barely think.
sceneCN: 这里 insomnia 是「失眠症」（第 2 个义项：持续多夜、已成病症的那种失眠）；句意为到了第三周，失眠已经把他拖得几乎无法思考。

forms.label: 不可数名词（通常无复数）

derivatives.zh: 失眠患者；由 insomnia 换 -ac（指人）构成，也可作形容词
失眠的；睡不着的；由拉丁语 insomnis 加 -ous 构成

senses.title: Sleeplessness
senses.definition: the condition of being awake when one wants to sleep, especially on one particular night
senses.definitionCN: 想睡却醒着的状态，尤指某一个夜里
senses.example: A bad cough gave him one night of insomnia.
senses.exampleCN: 一场剧烈的咳嗽让他失眠了一夜。
senses.why: Latin in- denies and somnus is sleep, so the word simply states the absence of sleep.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in- 表示否定，somnus 是睡眠，所以这个词只是直白地说「没有睡眠」。

senses.title: The persistent disorder
senses.definition: a lasting pattern of poor sleep that leaves a person tired and impaired during the day
senses.definitionCN: 长期睡不好、白天疲惫且状态受损的一种病症
senses.example: Insomnia is diagnosed when the problem lasts for weeks rather than for one night.
senses.exampleCN: 失眠持续数周而不是一夜时，才会被诊断为失眠症。
senses.why: Medicine turned the simple absence of sleep into a disorder once doctors saw that it persists and harms the day.
senses.whyCN: 当医生发现「睡不着」会持续下去并损害白天的状态，医学就把单纯的缺觉变成了一种病症。

senses.title: Trouble falling asleep
senses.definition: the form of insomnia in which a person lies awake for a long time before sleeping
senses.definitionCN: 躺了很久仍睡不着的那一类失眠
senses.example: Her insomnia begins at bedtime, when the lights go out.
senses.exampleCN: 她的失眠从熄灯上床那一刻开始。
senses.why: Because sleep has two gates, the word splits into a failure to enter sleep and a failure to stay in it.
senses.whyCN: 睡眠有两道门，这个词于是分成「进不去」和「待不住」两种情形。

senses.title: Waking in the night
senses.definition: the form of insomnia in which a person wakes repeatedly or too early and cannot sleep again
senses.definitionCN: 夜里反复醒来或醒得太早、再难入睡的那一类失眠
senses.example: His insomnia shows up at three in the morning, when he cannot fall back asleep.
senses.exampleCN: 他的失眠出现在凌晨三点，醒了就再难睡回去。
senses.why: Staying asleep is the second gate, and its failure earned the same name as the first.
senses.whyCN: 「睡得住」是第二道门，它失守时也用了同一个名字。

senses.title: Secondary insomnia
senses.definition: insomnia caused by another condition, such as pain, a drug or anxiety
senses.definitionCN: 由疼痛、药物或焦虑等其他状况引起的失眠
senses.example: The pain in his back brought on a secondary insomnia.
senses.exampleCN: 背痛引起了他的继发性失眠。
senses.why: When another illness keeps a patient awake, the sleeplessness becomes a symptom that borrows the name.
senses.whyCN: 当别的病让患者睡不着时，失眠就成了借用这个名字的一个症状。

intro.en: Insomnia is Latin in-, not, plus somnus, sleep: the word spells out its own meaning.
intro.cn: insomnia 是拉丁语 in-（不）加 somnus（睡眠）：这个词把自己的意思直接拼了出来。

items.en: Somnus named sleep, and the god of sleep carried the same name.
items.cn: somnus 指睡眠，睡神也用这个名字。

items.en: The prefix in- denied the word it joined, turning sleep into no sleep.
items.cn: 前缀 in- 否定它所接的词，把「睡眠」变成「没有睡眠」。

items.en: Insomnis described a person or a night without sleep.
items.cn: insomnis 形容不眠的人，也形容不眠的夜。

items.en: Insomnia turned the adjective into a noun naming sleeplessness itself.
items.cn: insomnia 把这个形容词变成名词，直接命名「睡不着」这件事。

items.en: English borrowed the Latin noun in the seventeenth century, at first for medical writing.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个拉丁名词，起初用于医学写作。

items.en: Sleep medicine later defined insomnia as a disorder with a duration and a daytime cost, not merely one bad night.
items.cn: 睡眠医学后来把失眠症定义为有持续时间、并带来白天代价的病症，而不只是一夜没睡好。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the Latin sleep root, and the near-meaning group separates insomnia from the tiredness and the sleep disorders around it.
note.cn: 形近组守住拉丁语「睡眠」这个词根；近义组把失眠与它周围的疲惫和睡眠疾病分开。

entries.definition: a person who rarely sleeps well, also used as an adjective
entries.definitionCN: 长期睡不好的人，也可作形容词；由 insomnia 换 -ac 构成。

entries.definition: sleepless or unable to sleep
entries.definitionCN: 失眠的；睡不着的；由拉丁语 insomnis 加 -ous 构成。

entries.definition: sleepy or inclined to sleep
entries.definitionCN: 困倦的、想睡的；与 insomnia 同出拉丁语 somnus（睡眠）。

entries.definition: the state of not sleeping, without implying a disorder
entries.definitionCN: 没睡着的状态，不暗示已成病症，范围比 insomnia 宽。

entries.definition: the condition that results from not getting enough sleep
entries.definitionCN: 睡眠不足造成的状态，是结果，而 insomnia 是原因。

entries.definition: a disorder in which a person falls asleep uncontrollably
entries.definitionCN: 无法控制地入睡的疾病，方向与失眠正好相反。

normalIntro.en: Insomnia is Latin in-, not, plus somnus, sleep, so the word form already carries its meaning.
normalIntro.cn: insomnia 是拉丁语 in-（不）加 somnus（睡眠），词形本身就已经带着它的意思。

normal.en: In- says not and somnus says sleep, so insomnia is literally no sleep.
normal.cn: in- 是「不」，somnus 是「睡眠」，insomnia 字面就是「没有睡眠」。

normal.en: Somnolent and somnambulist carry the same sleep root, one sleepy and one walking in sleep.
normal.cn: somnolent 与 somnambulist 共享同一个「睡眠」词根，一个指困倦，一个指梦游。

normal.en: An insomniac is the person, and insomnious is the rarer adjective for the sleepless state.
normal.cn: insomniac 指人，insomnious 是较少用的形容词，形容失眠的状态。

normal.en: Insomnia is uncountable, so a bout of insomnia names one episode.
normal.cn: insomnia 不可数，说 a bout of insomnia 才指一阵失眠。

normal.en: Sleep deprivation is the effect, while insomnia is the difficulty that causes it.
normal.cn: sleep deprivation 是结果，insomnia 则是造成它的那个困难。

abstract.en: Picture a clock above the bed, its hands moving while the eyes stay open.
abstract.cn: 想象床头上方有一只钟，指针在走，眼睛却一直睁着。

abstract.en: Imagine weeks of short nights and a face that grows grey in daylight.
abstract.cn: 想象连续数周夜夜短睡，一张脸在白天越来越灰。

abstract.en: Think of a body lying still while the mind keeps running through the day.
abstract.cn: 想象身体躺着不动，脑子却把白天的事一遍遍过。

examples.en: Insomnia made her dread the sound of the clock at night.
examples.cn: 失眠让她一到夜里就害怕听见钟声。

examples.en: He has struggled with insomnia since he changed jobs.
examples.cn: 换工作之后，他一直受失眠困扰。

examples.en: Doctors first treat insomnia by changing sleep habits.
examples.cn: 医生先通过改变睡眠习惯来治疗失眠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬睡么」——躺在床上硬要睡，偏偏睡不着，正好是这个意思；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ somnus（睡眠）→ insomnis（不眠的）→ insomnia（失眠）→ 英语直接借入，核心义「没有睡眠」。

sensesIntro.en: The word runs from one sleepless night to the lasting disorder, then splits into the two gates of sleep, and finally covers sleeplessness caused by something else.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一夜没睡，走到长期的病症，再分成睡眠的两道门，最后指由别的病引起的失眠。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clock above the bed moving all night while the eyes stay open.
core.cn: 核心意象：床头的钟走了一整夜，眼睛始终睁着。

branches.en: One sleepless night is the plain everyday sense.
branches.cn: 一夜没睡，是最日常的义项。

branches.en: The lasting disorder is the medical sense.
branches.cn: 长期存在的病症，是医学义项。

branches.en: Failing to enter sleep is the first of the two gates.
branches.cn: 进不了睡眠，是两道门中的第一道。

branches.en: Waking in the night is the other gate.
branches.cn: 夜里醒来，是另一道门。

branches.en: A single bad night and sleeplessness caused by pain share one word.
branches.cn: 一夜没睡好，与疼痛引起的失眠，共用一个词。

intro.en: Insomnia is Latin in- plus somnus, and the same stem returns in insomniac, insomnious and somnolent.
intro.cn: insomnia 是拉丁语 in- 加 somnus，同一个词干还出现在 insomniac、insomnious 与 somnolent 里。

latinIntro.en: Latin somnus means sleep, insomnis means sleepless, and insomnia names the condition itself.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 somnus 是睡眠，insomnis 是不眠的，insomnia 则命名这种状态本身。

latinEntries.exampleCN: somnus 生出 somnolent 与 insomnia。

latinEntries.example: Insomnis is the adjective behind insomnia.
latinEntries.exampleCN: insomnis 是 insomnia 背后的那个形容词。
somnium 生出 somnial 与 somnium。

definition_zh: 诊断；诊断结论；诊断过程
definition_en: the work of identifying a disease from its signs and symptoms, or the name given to that disease
core_image: 散落一桌的症状碎片，被拼成一张写着病名的标签
scene: 医生把化验单、听诊记录和影像片子并排摊在桌上，一条条对照。After three days of tests, the diagnosis was still unclear.
sceneCN: 这里 diagnosis 是「诊断结论」（第 2 个义项：给病情定名的那句结论）；句意为检查做了三天，诊断结论仍不清楚。

derivatives.zh: 诊断；由 diagnosis 逆构而来的动词
诊断的；来自希腊语 diagnōstikos，也可作名词指诊断试剂
诊断医师；diagnostic 加 -ian 指以此为业的人
诊断学；作不可数名词，指诊断的技术与流程

senses.title: The process of identifying a disease
senses.definition: the steps by which a doctor gathers signs, symptoms and tests in order to name the condition
senses.definitionCN: 医生汇集体征、症状与检查结果，以确定病名的整个过程
senses.example: Diagnosis began with a careful history and a physical examination.
senses.exampleCN: 诊断从详细的病史和体格检查开始。
senses.why: Greek dia- means through or apart and gnosis means knowledge, so diagnosis is knowledge worked out by sifting.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 dia- 表示「穿过、分开」，gnosis 表示「知」，所以诊断就是靠分辨筛出来的那种「知」。

senses.title: The named conclusion
senses.definition: the opinion or label that names the disease after the evidence has been weighed
senses.definitionCN: 权衡证据之后为疾病定名的那条结论
senses.example: The final diagnosis was pneumonia rather than a virus.
senses.exampleCN: 最终诊断是肺炎，而不是病毒感染。
senses.why: Once the sifting ends, the same word names the answer itself and not only the search.
senses.whyCN: 分辨结束之后，同一个词就指那个答案本身，而不只是指寻找的过程。

senses.title: Differential diagnosis
senses.definition: the systematic comparison of several possible diseases before one of them is chosen
senses.definitionCN: 在选定一种病之前，系统比较几种可能疾病的做法
senses.example: A differential diagnosis listed four diseases and ruled out three.
senses.exampleCN: 鉴别诊断列出四种病，又排除了其中三种。
senses.why: Because dia- also means apart, the word naturally covers the act of telling candidate diseases apart.
senses.whyCN: 因为 dia- 也有「分开」的意思，这个词自然就涵盖了把几种候选疾病区分开来的做法。

senses.title: A figurative assessment
senses.definition: a careful judgement about what is wrong with a system, an organization or an economy
senses.definitionCN: 对某个系统、机构或经济哪里出了问题的审慎判断
senses.example: The engineer gave a diagnosis of the failing network before any repair.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在动手修之前，先给这个出故障的网络下了一个诊断。
senses.why: The medical word was borrowed because every fault, like an illness, has to be named before it can be treated.
senses.whyCN: 医学词被借走，是因为任何故障都像疾病，必须先被命名才能被处理。

senses.title: Retrospective diagnosis
senses.definition: an attempt to name the illness of a person long dead, or of an event already past
senses.definitionCN: 为早已去世的人或已经过去的事推断病名的做法
senses.example: Historians still argue about the retrospective diagnosis of the last illness of the composer.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学者至今仍在争论这位作曲家临终所患何病的推断诊断。
senses.why: Because the tool outlived the clinic, it now reaches back into history, where the patient can no longer be examined.
senses.whyCN: 因为这件工具活过了诊室本身，它如今伸进历史，去面对再也无法受检的病人。

intro.en: Diagnosis joins Greek dia-, through or apart, to gnosis, knowledge, from the verb gignoskein, to know.
intro.cn: diagnosis 把希腊语 dia-（穿过、分开）与 gnosis（知）接在一起，后者来自动词 gignoskein（认识）。

items.en: Dia- meant through, and it also meant apart, as in separating one thing from another.
items.cn: dia- 意为「穿过」，也有「分开」的意思，如把一物与另一物分开。

items.en: Gignoskein meant to know or to recognize, especially to recognize a person.
items.cn: gignoskein 意为「知道、认出」，尤指认出一个人。

items.en: Gnosis was knowledge, and it became the second half of many learned words.
items.cn: gnosis 是「知识」，后来成了许多学术词的后半截。

items.en: Diagnosis meant a distinguishing or a discerning, the act of telling one thing from another.
items.cn: diagnosis 意为「辨别、辨识」，即把一物与另一物区分开的那个动作。

items.en: Medical Latin adopted the Greek noun, and it entered the European languages through medicine.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语采用了这个希腊名词，它又经由医学进入欧洲诸语言。

items.en: English took the word in the seventeenth century, first for medical judgement and later for any assessment.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪取用这个词，起初指医学判断，后来也指任何评估。

note.en: The look-alike group stays with the knowing root and its prefixed relatives, while the near-meaning group places diagnosis among the steps of clinical work.
note.cn: 形近组围绕「知」这个词根及其带前缀的同族词；近义组把诊断放进临床工作的各个环节里。

entries.definition: to identify a disease from its signs and symptoms
entries.definitionCN: 根据体征与症状辨认疾病；由 diagnosis 逆构出的动词。

entries.definition: used for or relating to diagnosis
entries.definitionCN: 用于诊断的、与诊断有关的；也可作名词指诊断试剂。

entries.definition: a forecast of how an illness is likely to develop
entries.definitionCN: 对病情发展的预测；与 diagnosis 同出 gnosis，前缀 pro- 表示「在前」。

entries.definition: the careful judging of a condition or a situation
entries.definitionCN: 对状况或处境的仔细评估，范围比 diagnosis 宽。

entries.definition: testing people for a disease before symptoms appear
entries.definitionCN: 在症状出现之前筛查疾病，是诊断之前的一步。

entries.definition: the physical checking of the body by a doctor
entries.definitionCN: 医生对身体做的检查，是诊断的依据之一，本身不是结论。

normalIntro.en: Diagnosis is built from dia-, through or apart, and gnosis, knowledge, so the word means knowledge sorted out by comparison.
normalIntro.cn: diagnosis 由 dia-（穿过、分开）与 gnosis（知）构成，所以这个词的意思是靠比较分拣出来的「知」。

normal.en: Dia- means through or apart and gnosis means knowledge, so diagnosis is knowledge gained by sifting.
normal.cn: dia- 是穿过或分开，gnosis 是知，diagnosis 就是靠分拣得来的认识。

normal.en: Diagnose is the verb, diagnosis the noun, and diagnostic the adjective.
normal.cn: diagnose 是动词，diagnosis 是名词，diagnostic 是形容词。

normal.en: The plural is diagnoses, with a long ee sound before the final s.
normal.cn: 复数是 diagnoses，末尾的 s 之前是一个长长的「伊」音。

normal.en: A differential diagnosis compares candidates before one of them is chosen.
normal.cn: differential diagnosis 先比较几种候选病，再从中选定一种。

normal.en: Prognosis shares gnosis but looks forward, while diagnosis looks at the present.
normal.cn: prognosis 共享 gnosis，却朝前看；diagnosis 看的是当下。

abstract.en: Picture scattered clues on a desk being fitted together into one label.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上散落的线索被拼成一张标签。

abstract.en: Imagine a long report with a single disease name written at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一长页报告的末尾只写着一个病名。

abstract.en: Think of three names on a whiteboard with two of them crossed out.
abstract.cn: 想象白板上写着三个病名，其中两个被划掉。

examples.en: The diagnosis was confirmed by a biopsy the next week.
examples.cn: 诊断在下一周由活检得到确认。

examples.en: Doctors need several tests before they can make a diagnosis.
examples.cn: 医生需要几项检查才能作出诊断。

examples.en: A delayed diagnosis can cost a patient the best window for treatment.
examples.cn: 诊断延迟可能让患者错过最好的治疗时机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「点个脑细思」——医生点着化验单，细细思量一番，才写下诊断；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 dia-（穿过、分开）+ gignōskein（认识）→ gnōsis（知识）→ diagnosis（辨别、判断）→ 拉丁语 diagnosis → 英语 diagnosis，核心义「把病情分辨清楚」。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from the sifting process to the named answer, then to the comparison of candidates, to any assessment outside medicine, and finally to a judgement about the past.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从分辨的过程走到定名的答案，再走到候选病的比较，又借到医学之外的任何评估，最后指向对往事的判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scattered clues fitted together into one label bearing a disease name.
core.cn: 核心意象：散落的线索被拼成一张写着病名的标签。

branches.en: The sifting process is the first sense of the word.
branches.cn: 分辨的过程，是这个词的第一个义项。

branches.en: The named answer is what the process produces.
branches.cn: 定名的答案，是这个过程产出的结果。

branches.en: Comparing candidates is the process at its most explicit.
branches.cn: 比较候选病，是这个过程最明确的形态。

branches.en: Outside medicine the same word assesses any faulty system.
branches.cn: 出了医学，同一个词用来评估任何出故障的系统。

branches.en: Both the clinic and the history book use the word for naming an illness from evidence.
branches.cn: 诊室与史书都用这个词，指根据证据为疾病定名。

intro.en: Diagnosis joins Greek dia- to gnosis, and English built diagnose, diagnostic and diagnostician on the same stem.
intro.cn: diagnosis 把希腊语 dia- 与 gnosis 接在一起，英语又用同一词干造出 diagnose、diagnostic 与 diagnostician。

latinIntro.en: Latin kept the Greek diagnosis and supplied cognoscere, to know, from the same deep knowing root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语保留了希腊语的 diagnosis，并提供 cognoscere（认识），它与这个词根同出更古老的「知」。

latinEntries.example: Diagnosis is the Latin form of the Greek noun.
latinEntries.exampleCN: diagnosis 是那个希腊名词的拉丁形式。
cognoscere 生出 cognition 与 recognise。
